newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Bulls boost Brussels bourse, but bears abroad.
newsitem.headline: Bulls boost Brussels bourse, but bears abroad.

text.p: Continued underlying bullish sentiment lifted the Brussels bourse in lacklustre dealings on Thursday, but traders said there were growing nerves over how long the market could maintain its upward impetus.
"It is becoming more of a lottery," one trader remarked. "Fundamentally nothing has changed, but just because the Fed didn't raise rates on Tuesday does not mean it won't in future."
"We will continue to follow other European markets which in turn are following the U.S.. The market is increasingly influenced by the weekly drip feed of U.S. statistics," the trader added.
The Bel-20 index of blue chip shares was up 4.12 points or 0.18 percent at 2,251.95 by 0920 GMT, with five gainers, seven unchanged and eight losers.
A total of just under 800 million francs of Belgian shares had changed hands.

Main gainer was Kredietbank, up 1.6 percent at 6,700 francs. Traders said it was being boosted by a report in weekly business magazine Trends that it was in discreet cooperation talks with Dutch Rabobank.
Kredietbank had no immediate comment on the report.
Broad-based holding company Ackermans & van Haaren was 4.05 percent up at 7,200, but traders said they were at a loss to explain the share's sudden strength.
Elsewhere the market had little specific focus, with a combination of bargain hunting and profit-taking keeping the index in a tight range.
